notes.title: DON'T! FRET - WE ARE MAKING GREAT PROGRESS!
notes.content:
[h1]Dear Community,[/h1][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44910425/f03ab15b487a0ad8b826560971bb7c88b0d7654d.png[/img]

Hey everyone!

It’s been a little while since our last official Steam Hub post, so thank you for your patience and continued interest in Don't! Fret. If you haven't already, be sure to join our Discord for more frequent updates and behind-the-scenes content:
👉 https://discord.gg/vHkv6HQztB

We recently released a detailed devlog video with tons of new info on development progress. You can check it out here:
[previewyoutube=t_DtsFYVzhQ;leftthumb][/previewyoutube]

[h1]UPDATES[/h1]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44910425/d11786e1dddcf18c037776fa22617948cb7405f2.png[/img]
We’re actively playtesting the first third of Don't! Fret!
All core gameplay mechanics are now complete.
Our main enemy, Tapehead, has undergone a major overhaul — and Fret has received some updates too.
We’ve created a brand-new, redesigned capsule art that better represents the game’s vibe and characters. Can’t wait to share it with you soon!
The current playtime for the first third of the game is averaging 1.5 hours, which means you can expect the full game to be around 4–5 hours long.
We've decided to make all cutscenes in-engine, resulting in a more seamless and immersive experience.
[h1]GAMEPLAY UPDATES[/h1]

You may have seen this mentioned on other platforms, but for those who haven't: the demo was just a tiny peek at Don't! Fret's atmosphere and tone — the final game is significantly more robust and polished in terms of gameplay.

Our original inspiration was to capture the intense, cat-and-mouse style of Alien: Isolation. And while we're a small team with limited resources, I truly believe we've built something that captures that same kind of tension.

The gameplay now blends elements of Resident Evil, Silent Hill, and Alien: Isolation.
The demo’s AI was very basic — “run-at-the-player” style — but that's completely changed. We’re spending a ton of time refining enemy behavior and making every encounter feel fun, tense, and rewarding.

[h1]VARIETY[/h1][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44910425/7b101727ea3fdb7fb8581b9542827ebb15477274.png[/img]

One of the things I’m most proud of is the variety in Don't! Fret.

Yes, the game is set in a school — but trust me when I say, it’s a wild ride of constantly evolving environments and surprising set pieces. We’re working hard to make sure each area feels distinct and keeps you on your toes.

When I say varied, I really mean it.

[h1]RELEASE DATE[/h1]

We’ve made the decision to move our release window to early 2026.

This gives us the time we need to avoid crunch, polish the experience, and make sure Don't! Fret is the best it can possibly be when it reaches you.

[h1]THANK YOU[/h1]

Thank you all so much for your continued support. It means the world to our team.

If you haven’t already, come hang out with us on Discord — we’d love to chat and keep you in the loop as we get closer to release!

See you soon,
💀 Scary Kid Studios

notes.title: PATCH 1.1 - Performance Optimization & Xbox Controller Support
notes.content:
[b]CPU & GPU Performance Optimization[/b]
50% frame increase
Significantly reduced draw calls
Reduced total triangles visible on screen
LOD optimization
Batched static mesh throughout the map
GPU optimization with particle effects

[b]Xbox Controller Support[/b]
Xbox controller support
NOTE: There are known issues with keypad losing movement with controller. If this happens, you can use your mouse and keyboard to progress
NOTE: PS5 and Steam Deck support is not fully compatible yet but is on the horizon

[b]Added additional frame limits[/b]
Increased frame limit cap to 144

[b]Bug Fixes[/b]
Player can no longer interact with light switch from inside of Waste Room
Pressing wrong number on payphone no longer results in an infinite dial
Player can no longer move during cut scenes after first playthrough
Fixed issue where player can press reload on flashlight and begin to use it before animation is completed
Fixed issue where interacting with machine or cassette player would allow you to use an item without being near it

[b]Known Issues[/b]
Xbox controller input issues where controller loses input for certain objects like keypad, payphone
No PS4 or PS5 controller support
No Steam Deck Support
